The engineer works with the Linux Vulnerability Engineer to prioritize patching based on risk and customer requirements, and with the Patching Automation Engineer to automate what can be automated. The role also partners with Linux and Unix administrators, application owners, change management, service delivery, and the Windows and Middleware Patching Engineers. The Linux Patching Engineer owns patch execution and outcomes; the Patching Automation Engineer builds and maintains reusable automation. Track Red Hat Security Advisories and vendor errata; with the Linux Vulnerability Engineer, prioritize patches by severity, exploitability, system criticality, operational risk, and customer requirements; and maintain routine and emergency schedules aligned with SLAs and maintenance requirements. Manage patch content in Red Hat Satellite or an equivalent platform (content views, lifecycle environments, repository snapshots) to give each environment a tested, consistent baseline. Review errata, dependencies, and known issues; coordinate testing across development, test, staging, disaster recovery, and production, accounting for application compatibility, third-party agents and kernel modules, and high-availability clusters such as Pacemaker. Prepare implementation, validation, communication, and backout plans; maintain change records (risk assessments, approvals, test evidence, affected systems); and confirm backup and recovery readiness before deployment. Lead patch readiness and go/no-go reviews; coordinate deployments and reboot sequencing in approved windows, apply kernel live patches where supported, and verify systems, applications, services, and clusters afterward. Troubleshoot package conflicts, repository errors, failed kernel updates, and post-patch boot or service issues; coordinate rollback or recovery, escalate service-impacting failures, and apply lessons learned to future cycles. Manage patch exceptions, including end-of-life or extended-support systems; document compensating controls and remediation plans, and retain approval, testing, deployment, and remediation evidence for audits. Work with the Patching Automation Engineer to automate what can be automated, defining, testing, and validating Linux patching workflows (Ansible playbooks, Satellite remote execution jobs, controls, exception handling, recovery) while retaining ownership of execution, compliance, and remediation outcomes. Maintain patch calendars, runbooks, inventories, and dashboards; report compliance, deployment status, failures, exceptions, aging vulnerabilities, and risks; and coordinate shared maintenance windows with the Windows and Middleware Patching Engineers.
